messages:
maria_support: FYI customer (acct: redwood-corp) flagged a big drop in reserved GPU hours showing on their dashboard after SLA credits were applied, but their invoice still charged full commit. They say token usage was low during window. Can we triage?

aj_billing: thanks, maria. can you paste the pool id + invoice line item id? also any dashboard screenshot/time range?

maria_support: pool id: pool-42-eu; invoice line: inv-2026-07-LN3. screenshot attached in support ticket but summary: dashboard shows reserved_hours used = 5.2 for 2026-07-12 00:00-06:00 UTC, invoice shows 48 commit hours billed. customer claims SLA credit applied but net still off.

aj_billing: ok pulling meter logs. initial thought: attribution mismatch between billed commit hours (hourly rounding) vs dashboard hourly aggregation. will check raw meter events.

ken_infra: I see a burst of prewarm probes hitting pool-42 at 2026-07-12T03:11:40Z -> 03:13:05Z. Logs: "probe: prewarm check" repeated; each probe creates a transient allocation that increments committed_hours counter in metering pipeline. snippet: ```
2026-07-12T03:11:40Z INFO probe prewarm pool=pool-42 probe_id=pr-998 duration_ms=1200
2026-07-12T03:12:03Z INFO probe prewarm pool=pool-42 probe_id=pr-999 duration_ms=900
```

sophia_prod: that period also had a fallback routing event where requests from eu-hosted app routed to dedicated-burst variant (pool-42-burst) while pool-42 was scaling. fallback policy logs: route -> burst on saturate. those burst allocations are expected to be billed to burst bucket, not commit. need to confirm mapping to invoice line.

aj_billing: looking at raw meter_events for pool-42 between 03:00-04:00 UTC. we have two classes of events: "commit_allocation_start" and "probe_allocation_start". invoice aggregation job currently maps commit* -> reserved_line_item, probe* -> reserved_line_item as well because probe type wasn't whitelisted in the invoicing schema. that explains why probes inflated billed hours.

maria_support: customer says token burn was ~12k tokens in that 6h window. if actual token usage low, the commit hours charge felt disproportionate. they want a credit + root cause.

aj_billing: proposed short fix: change invoicing mapper to treat probe_* events as non-billable or bill to prewarm credits. longer term: add rule: if event.source=="probe" and duration_ms<5000 -> attribute to warmup_credits and exclude from reserved commit total. will open PR.

ken_infra: quick repro steps if you want to validate locally: run a scripted probe loop against pool-42: ```
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Pool: pool-42" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  sleep 1
done
``` these create probe allocations in our current runtime. watch metering stream via: `kubectl logs -f metering-processor | grep pool-42`

sophia_prod: also note fallback->burst routing creates short-lived worker VMs that were previously flagged as "burst" in metering. a recent change to the metering schema consolidated burst/probe into generic "allocation" which lost the original tag. need to restore the allocation.tag field through the metrics pipeline.

aj_billing: I've located the invoice delta: inv-2026-07-LN3 shows 48.0 billed commit hours, but raw commit_allocation_start/stop only sum to ~5.2h. additional ~43h came from 2,6k probe events that were incorrectly mapped.

maria_support: customer asked for interim credit while we fix mapping. what do we need from finance/legal to issue a one-off adjustment?

lucas_account: I'll escalate to finance. prep a doc with exact hours to reverse + proposed SLA credit amount. we should also confirm whether the customer used burst capacity legitimately — if they did, we might bill burst usage instead of reversing commit charges.

aj_billing: next steps I will: 1) open billing-mapper PR to exclude probe_* from reserved commit mapping (refs: GH#billing/mapper PR #512) 2) backfill invoice corrections for inv-2026-07-LN3 with a credit of ~43h (TBD by finance) 3) provide a traceable audit (sql query) used to compute the delta: ```
SELECT event_type, SUM(duration_seconds)/3600 as hours
FROM metering_events
WHERE pool_id='pool-42' AND ts >= '2026-07-12T00:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-07-13T00:00:00Z'
GROUP BY event_type;
```

ken_infra: I've also added a small patch to runtime to tag probe allocations with allocation.tag=probe before they hit metering so we can make the mapper deterministic. deploying to canary in eu region now (job id: deploy-2107-probe-tag).

sophia_prod: track as follow-up in product backlog: ensure any consolidation of allocation types preserves upstream billing tags. I'll create a ticket with acceptance criteria.

billing-bot: Billing event detected: inv-2026-07-LN3 adjustment requested by @aj_billing. Ticket: BILL-8792 created.

maria_support: thanks everyone. i've updated the customer that we're issuing a provisional credit and will follow up once finance confirms final amount. closing loop once adjustment posts. :thumbsup:

aj_billing: FYI I'll post the PR link and the final audit query results in this thread once backfill runs.

lucas_account: noted, I'll coordinate the invoice credit and send the revised statement to the customer once posted.

(END)
